description: Fully autonomous AI Agents system capable of performing complex penetration testing tasks
vibe: Comments are a budget, not a diary — spend them only on what the code cannot say.
highlights: Comment density targets: 0–2% of a logic file, ~18% of a type-declaration file; hundreds-line function bodies carry none.
A comment must carry why-this-not-the-obvious, external constraints, or boundary conditions — never restate the code.
No archaeology: git holds history, so 'it used to be' and 'no longer' are deleted while the invariant they protected stays.
No dead pointers: no §, no requirement ids like (R37), no references to untracked planning documents.
GraphQL schema is a public artifact — zero triple-quoted descriptions, fields never commented, names must speak for themselves.
Comment-only changes are proven by comparing comment-free token streams (go/scanner, ts.createPrinter) rather than reading diffs.
assessment: This file treats comments as a scarce engineering resource with measurable budgets and explicit deletion criteria, which is rare and unusually disciplined. The distinction between machine-read comments (swaggo annotations, sqlc name comments, GraphQL descriptions) and human prose shows a systems-level understanding of where text actually travels. The insistence on proving comment-only changes via token-stream comparison, including validating the checker in both directions, is the kind of rigor that prevents silent regressions in refactors.
